pages.title: What Is Waste?
pages.content:
Every day, we eat food and drink water. We use bottles, boxes and bags. Then we throw away these things. This is waste.

There is a lot of waste in the world. In 2023, people in cities made more than 2 billion tons of waste. In 2050, there will be about 4 billion tons!

A lot of waste is food. There is a lot of paper and plastic, too. But many old things are good. We can use them again.

vocabulary.definition: Put something in the bin.
Things we do not want or need.
1 ton is 1,000 kilograms.

pages.title: Paper, Wood and Glass
pages.content:
Paper and wood come from trees. We can recycle old paper. Then we can make new paper and new boxes. This is good for the trees. Old paper goes in a paper bin.

We can make new things from old wood, too.

Glass comes from sand. Old glass bottles and jars go in a glass bin. Workers put the green, brown and white glass in groups. They make it very hot. Then they make new bottles and jars.

vocabulary.definition: The hard part of a tree.
A box for waste.
Make new things from old things.
Small yellow pieces on a beach.
Glass boxes for food, like honey.
People at work.

pages.title: Plastic and the Sea
pages.content:
Plastic is in many things. Bags, bottles, pens and phones have plastic in them.

In 2019, there were about 350 million tons of plastic waste in the world. People recycled only 9 percent of it. Half of it went under the ground. A lot of it went into rivers and the sea.

Plastic in the sea is very bad. Fish and birds eat it, and they get ill. We should help the seas. We shouldn't throw plastic on the beach.

vocabulary.definition: A light, strong material for bags and bottles.
A part of 100; 50 percent is half.
The earth under our feet.

pages.title: Cartons, Cans and Oil
pages.content:
Juice and milk cartons have paper and plastic in them. Workers take out the paper and the plastic. Then they make new things.

Drink cans are metal. Workers make old metal very hot. Then they make new things from it.

After we cook food, we have old oil. It is waste, too. We mustn't put it in the water. It is bad for the water. Workers change it into fuel for cars.

vocabulary.definition: Paper boxes for milk or juice.
Metal boxes for drinks or food.
A hard material, like iron.
A liquid from plants for cooking.
Cars need it to move.

pages.title: Food Waste
pages.content:
A lot of food is waste. Some food never comes to the shops. Some food goes in the bin at home, in restaurants and in shops.

Where is a lot of food waste? It is at home! 61 percent of all food waste is in our homes. We buy a lot of food. Then some of it goes bad.

We should buy only the food that we need. We should eat our old bread first.

vocabulary.definition: Not good to eat.

pages.title: Old Phones and Batteries
pages.content:
We have a lot of machines at home and at school. Phones, computers and TVs help us every day. Sometimes they are old or broken. Then they are waste.

Old machines go in a different bin. Workers open them. They can use the metal and the plastic again.

Batteries make games, phones and clocks work. Old batteries are dangerous. We mustn't throw them in the kitchen bin. They go in a battery bin.

vocabulary.definition: Phones, computers, TVs and other things like them.
Not working.
Small things that make phones and clocks work.
Bad for people and nature.

pages.title: Zero Waste and the Three Rs
pages.content:
What is Zero Waste? It is not "no waste". Every person makes some waste every day. Zero Waste is less waste. We use things again and again.

Here are the three Rs of Zero Waste:

Reduce: Use less. Buy only the things that you need.

Reuse and Repair: Use things again. When something is broken, repair it.

Recycle: Make new things from old things.

Old things can be new things again.

vocabulary.definition: A way of life with less waste.
Not as much.
Use less.
Use again.
Make a broken thing good again.

pages.title: What Can We Do?
pages.content:
Food in the ground makes a bad gas. This gas makes our world hotter. With less waste, there is less gas.

The best waste is the waste that we never make. We can all help. Take a bag from home to the shop. Take a bottle and a cup from home to school. Say "no" to plastic straws.

Cities can help, too. Some cities have tool libraries. People can take tools from there, and they do not need to buy them.

Families can learn about Zero Waste together. The best time to start is now!

vocabulary.definition: Something like air; we cannot see it.
A glass or plastic thing for water.
Thin plastic tubes for drinks.
Places where you can take tools and bring them back.
